Participant demographics

# Extract sample metadata
metadata <- as.data.frame(colData(tse))

# Convert categories to factor variables
metadata$Sex <- as.factor(metadata$Sex)
metadata$Giardia <- as.factor(metadata$Giardia)
metadata$abx_6mo <- as.factor(metadata$abx_6mo)
metadata$daily_water_contact <- as.factor(metadata$daily_water_contact)
metadata$latrine_defaecation <- as.factor(metadata$latrine_defaecation)
metadata$Piped_water <- ifelse(metadata$drinking_water == "Piped", "Yes", "No")
metadata$Piped_water <- as.factor(metadata$Piped_water)
# Age
summary(metadata$Age)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   6.000   7.000  10.000   9.694  12.250  15.000
# Categorical variable summaries
categorical_vars <- c(
  "Sex",
  "Giardia",
  "abx_6mo",
  "Piped_water",
  "daily_water_contact",
  "latrine_defaecation"
)

# Generate summary of categorical variables
lapply(categorical_vars, function(v) {
  metadata %>%
    dplyr::count(.data[[v]]) %>%
    mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
})

Check for differences between groups

# Age
kruskal.test(Age ~ Category, data = metadata)
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  Age by Category
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 0.018872, df = 2, p-value = 0.9906
# Sex
sex_tab <- table(
  metadata$Sex,
  metadata$Category
)

fisher.test(sex_tab)
## 
##  Fisher's Exact Test for Count Data
## 
## data:  sex_tab
## p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
# Giardiasis
giardiasis_tab <- table(
  metadata$Giardia,
  metadata$Category
)

fisher.test(giardiasis_tab)
## 
##  Fisher's Exact Test for Count Data
## 
## data:  giardiasis_tab
## p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
# Antibiotics
abx_tab <- table(
  metadata$abx_6mo,
  metadata$Category
)

fisher.test(abx_tab)
## 
##  Fisher's Exact Test for Count Data
## 
## data:  abx_tab
## p-value = 0.5757
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
# Piped drinking water
piped_tab <- table(
  metadata$Piped_water,
  metadata$Category
)

fisher.test(piped_tab)
## 
##  Fisher's Exact Test for Count Data
## 
## data:  piped_tab
## p-value = 0.3336
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
# Daily environmental water contact
env_water_tab <- table(
  metadata$daily_water_contact,
  metadata$Category
)

fisher.test(env_water_tab)
## 
##  Fisher's Exact Test for Count Data
## 
## data:  env_water_tab
## p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
# Latrine use for defaecation
latrine_tab <- table(
  metadata$latrine_defaecation,
  metadata$Category
)

fisher.test(latrine_tab)
## 
##  Fisher's Exact Test for Count Data
## 
## data:  latrine_tab
## p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided

Taxonomy

# Calculate the number of unique taxa for each taxonomic rank
apply(rowData(tse), 2, function (x) {length(unique(x))})
##    kingdom     phylum      class      order     family      genus    species 
##          1         19        338        354        387       1016       1575 
##     strain clade_name 
##       1610       1610
# Extract a presence/absence matrix for species-level genome bins (SGBs)
pa <- assay(tse) > 0

# Identify how many SGBs are shared between samples (pairwise)
shared_mat <- t(pa) %*% pa

# Calculate the number of SGBs identified in all samples
shared_all <- sum(rowSums(pa) == ncol(pa))
shared_all
## [1] 36
# Calculate the minimum number of SBGs shared between two participants
min_shared <- min(shared_mat[upper.tri(shared_mat)])
min_shared
## [1] 94
# Calculate the maximum number of SBGs shared between two participants
max_shared <- max(shared_mat[upper.tri(shared_mat)])
max_shared
## [1] 568
# Identify the SBGs identified in >20% of samples (minimum 8 samples), to be used downstream for StrainPhlAn profiling

# Number of samples in which each SGB is present
sgb_n_samples <- rowSums(pa, na.rm = TRUE)

# Threshold: >20% of 36 samples = >=8 samples
min_samples <- 8

# Vector of SGB IDs passing the threshold
sgbs_keep <- rownames(pa)[sgb_n_samples >= min_samples]

# Export list
writeLines(sgbs_keep, "Data/main_sgbs.txt")

NB. Using this identified list of SGBs, StrainPhlAn was run.

Phyla

# Make a new TSE for phylum

# Plot abundance
phylum_plot <- plotAbundance(
  tse_phylum,
  assay.type = "relabundance",
  rank = "phylum",
  order.col.by = "Order",
  add_x_text = TRUE
) +
  labs(y = "Relative abundance") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = custom_phyla_colors,
    breaks = names(custom_phyla_colors),
    labels = custom_phyla_labels,
    name = "Phylum"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = NA), ncol = 2)) +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6)
  )
## Scale for fill is already present.
## Adding another scale for fill, which will replace the existing scale.
# Save the plot
ggsave("Figures/phylum_plot.png", plot = phylum_plot, width = 11, height = 4, dpi = 600)

# Make a relative abundance matrix for phyla
relabundance_matrix_phylum <- assay(altExp(tse, "phylum"), "mpa")

# Calculate the mean relative abundance of each phylum
mean_relabundance_phylum <- rowMeans(relabundance_matrix_phylum)

# Sort from highest to lowest
mean_relabundance_phylum <- sort(mean_relabundance_phylum, decreasing = TRUE)

# Print the mean relative abundance of each phylum
mean_relabundance_phylum

Orders

# Make a relative abundance matrix for orders
relabundance_matrix_order <- assay(altExp(tse, "order"), "mpa")

# Calculate the total relative abundance of each order (row sums)
total_relabundance_order <- rowSums(relabundance_matrix_order)

# Identify the top 20 orders
top_orders <- names(sort(total_relabundance_order, decreasing = TRUE)[1:20])

# Make a new TSE for top 20 orders
tse_top_20_orders <- altExp(tse, "order")
tse_top_20_orders <- transformAssay(tse_top_20_orders, assay.type = "mpa", method = "relabundance")
rowData(tse_top_20_orders)$order <- ifelse(rowData(tse_top_20_orders)$order %in% top_orders, rowData(tse_top_20_orders)$order, "-Other")

Hierarchical clustering of samples and taxa

# Generate order TSE
tse_order <- altExp(tse, "order")
tse_order <- transformAssay(tse_order, assay.type = "mpa", method = "relabundance")

# Add clr-transformation
tse_order <- transformAssay(tse_order, assay.type = "relabundance",
                              method = "clr", pseudocount = TRUE)
## A pseudocount of 1.49999955000014e-07 was applied.
# Apply a z-transformation across rows (taxa)
tse_order <- transformAssay(tse_order, assay.type = "clr", 
                              MARGIN = "features",
                              method = "standardize", name = "clr_z")

# Get 50 most abundant orders and subset the data by them
top_50_orders <- names(sort(total_relabundance_order, decreasing = TRUE)[1:50])
tse_order_subset <- tse_order[top_50_orders, ]

# Calculate the proportion accounted for in the top 50 Orders
(sum(assay(tse_order_subset, "relabundance"))) / 36
## [1] 0.9221749
# Gets the assay table
mat <- assay(tse_order_subset, "clr_z")

# Make a dataframe for taxonomic information
taxonomic_data <- as.data.frame(rowData(tse_order_subset))
taxonomic_data <- taxonomic_data[, "phylum", drop = FALSE]
colnames(taxonomic_data)[colnames(taxonomic_data) == "phylum"] <- "Phylum"
taxonomic_data$Phylum <- gsub("^p__", "", taxonomic_data$Phylum)
taxonomic_data$Phylum <- gsub("_", " ", taxonomic_data$Phylum)
rownames(taxonomic_data) <- sub("s_G", "s G", rownames(taxonomic_data))
rownames(mat) <- sub("s_G", "s G", rownames(mat))

# Make a dataframe for sample information
sample_data <- as.data.frame(colData(tse_order_subset))
sample_data <- sample_data[, c("Category", "Age", "Sex", "abx_6mo"), drop = FALSE]
names(sample_data)[names(sample_data) == "abx_6mo"] <- "Antibiotics in previous 6 months"

# Set heatmap scaling and colors
breaks <- seq(-ceiling(max(abs(mat))), ceiling(max(abs(mat))), 
              length.out = ifelse( max(abs(mat))>5, 2*ceiling(max(abs(mat))), 10 ) )
colors <- colorRampPalette(c("darkblue", "blue", "white", "red", "darkred"))(length(breaks)-1)

# Set column annotation colors
ann_colors <- list(
  Phylum = c(
    "Actinomycetota" = "greenyellow",
    "Bacteroidota" = "yellow2",
    "Campylobacterota" = "#1B9E77",
    "Candidatus Melainabacteria" = "#66C2A5",
    "Elusimicrobiota" = "#3288BD",
    "Firmicutes" = "#5E4FA2",
    "Lentisphaerota" = "#ABDDA4",
    "Mycoplasmatota" = "#A6CEE3",
    "Pseudomonadota" = "#8DA0CB",
    "Spirochaetota" = "#E0F3F8",
    "Thermodesulfobacteriota" = "#00441B"
  ),
  "Antibiotics in previous 6 months" = c(
    "Yes" = "red",
    "No" = "bisque"
  ),
  Sex = c(
    "Male" = "blue",
    "Female" = "lightblue"
  ),
  Category = c(
    "Control" = "grey90",
    "UGS" = "grey60",
    "ZIS" = "grey30"
  )
)

# Create the heatmap
order_clusters_with_metadata <- pheatmap(mat, annotation_col = sample_data, annotation_row = taxonomic_data, color = colors, annotation_colors = ann_colors, breaks = breaks, legend_width = 0.5)

# Save the plot
ggsave("Figures/order_clusters_with_metadata.png", plot = order_clusters_with_metadata, width = 12, height = 9, dpi = 600)

# Print plot
print(order_clusters_with_metadata)

Diversity

Alpha diversity

# Make a new TSE for species
tse_species <- altExp(tse, "species")
tse_species <- transformAssay(tse_species, assay.type = "mpa", method = "relabundance")

# Calculate diversity statistics
tse_species <- addAlpha(tse_species, index = "shannon", assay.type = "relabundance")
tse_species <- addAlpha(tse_species, index = "gini_simpson", assay.type = "relabundance")
tse_species <- addAlpha(tse_species, index = "observed_richness", assay.type = "relabundance")

Plot

# Prepare plotting data
alpha_df <- colData(tse_species) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Age = as.numeric(as.character(Age)),
    Sex = factor(
      Sex,
      levels = c("Female", "Male")
    )
  )

# Shared high-contrast age colour scale
age_colour_scale <- function() {
  scale_colour_viridis_c(
    option = "plasma",
    direction = 1,
    limits = c(6, 15),
    breaks = c(6, 15),
    labels = c("6", "15"),
    name = "Age",
    oob = scales::squish,
    guide = guide_colourbar(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      barwidth = grid::unit(4, "cm"),
      barheight = grid::unit(0.35, "cm")
    )
  )
}

# Shared shapes for sex
sex_shape_scale <- function() {
  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Sex",
    values = c(
      "Female" = 16,
      "Male" = 17
    ),
    guide = guide_legend(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE
    )
  )
}

# Shared plot function
make_alpha_plot <- function(
    data,
    y_variable,
    y_label,
    show_x_axis = FALSE
) {

  p <- ggplot(
    data,
    aes(
      x = Category,
      y = .data[[y_variable]]
    )
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(
      outlier.shape = NA,
      width = 0.6,
      alpha = 0.15,
      colour = "black"
    ) +
    ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(
      aes(
        colour = Age,
        shape = Sex
      ),
      width = 0.2,
      alpha = 0.65,
      size = 2
    ) +
    age_colour_scale() +
    sex_shape_scale() +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
        colour = "grey90",
        linewidth = 0.3
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
    )

  if (!show_x_axis) {
    p <- p +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank()
      )
  } else {
    p <- p +
      labs(
        x = "Schistosomiasis category"
      ) +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(
          angle = 10,
          hjust = 1
        )
      )
  }

  p
}

# Shannon diversity
p_shannon <- make_alpha_plot(
  data = alpha_df,
  y_variable = "shannon",
  y_label = "Shannon"
)

# Gini–Simpson diversity
p_gini <- make_alpha_plot(
  data = alpha_df,
  y_variable = "gini_simpson",
  y_label = "Gini–Simpson"
)

# Observed richness
p_rich <- make_alpha_plot(
  data = alpha_df,
  y_variable = "observed_richness",
  y_label = "Richness (no. species)",
  show_x_axis = TRUE
)

# Combined plot
alpha_diversity_plot <-
  p_shannon /
  p_gini /
  p_rich +
  patchwork::plot_layout(
    guides = "collect"
  ) &
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "horizontal"
  )

# Save the plot
ggsave(
  filename = "Figures/alpha_diversity_plot.png",
  plot = alpha_diversity_plot,
  width = 6.5,
  height = 6.5,
  dpi = 600
)

# Print the plot
print(alpha_diversity_plot)

Non-parametric statistical tests

Shannon

kruskal.test(tse_species[["shannon"]], tse_species[["Category"]])
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  tse_species[["shannon"]] and tse_species[["Category"]]
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 1.473, df = 2, p-value = 0.4788

Gini-Simpson

kruskal.test(tse_species[["gini_simpson"]], tse_species[["Category"]])
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  tse_species[["gini_simpson"]] and tse_species[["Category"]]
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 3.8574, df = 2, p-value = 0.1453

Richness

kruskal.test(tse_species[["observed_richness"]], tse_species[["Category"]])
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  tse_species[["observed_richness"]] and tse_species[["Category"]]
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 0.7042, df = 2, p-value = 0.7032

Thoughts… - Shannon diversity values fell within the expected range for age-matched pediatric populations, indicating no evidence of gross microbiome depletion associated with schistosomiasis status. - Any IS effect is likely subtle, taxon-specific, functional rather than ecological collapse

Beta diversity & dissimilarity

Species-level

# Make a new TSE for species

tse_species <- transformAssay(tse_species, assay.type = "mpa", method = "relabundance")

# Generate beta-diversity statistics (Bray-Curtis distance)
tse_species <- addDissimilarity(tse_species, assay.type = "relabundance" , method = "bray")
bray_data <- metadata(tse_species)[["bray"]]

PCoA

Taxonomic profiles
# Perform multidimensional scaling (MDS) using Bray-Curtis dissimilarity on relative abundance data at the species level
tse_species <- addMDS(
    tse_species, 
    FUN = getDissimilarity, 
    method = "bray", 
    assay.type = "relabundance", 
    name = "MDS_bray"
)

# Extract coordinates
mds_coords <- reducedDims(tse_species)$MDS_bray

# Calculate explained variance
e <- attr(reducedDims(tse_species)$MDS_bray, "eig")
rel_eig <- e / sum(e[e > 0])
axis1_pct <- round(100 * rel_eig[[1]], 1)
axis2_pct <- round(100 * rel_eig[[2]], 1)
print("axis1_pct")
## [1] "axis1_pct"
print(axis1_pct)
## [1] 14.9
print("axis2_pct")
## [1] "axis2_pct"
print(axis2_pct)
## [1] 9.2
# Create data frame for plotting
pcoa_df <- data.frame(
  Axis1 = mds_coords[,1],
  Axis2 = mds_coords[,2],
  SampleName = rownames(mds_coords)
)

# Add category to the data frame for plotting
pcoa_df$Category <- colData(tse_species)$Category

# Plot PCoA with 95% CI ellipses
pcoa_plot <- ggplot(
  pcoa_df,
  aes(x = Axis1, y = Axis2, color = Category)
) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(fill = Category),
               type = "t",
               level = 0.95,
               geom = "polygon",
               alpha = 0.15,
               color = NA) +
  stat_ellipse(type = "t", level = 0.95, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal"
    ) +
  labs(
    x = "PCoA 1 (14.9%)",
    y = "PCoA 2 (9.2%)",
    color = "Schistosomiasis category",
    fill = "Schistosomiasis category",
    title = "Species composition"
  )

# Add boxplots to display differences between groups
pcoa_plot <- ggMarginal(pcoa_plot, type = "boxplot", groupFill = TRUE)

# Save the plot
ggsave("Figures/pcoa_plot_taxonomic_profiles.png", pcoa_plot, width = 4.2, height = 3.5)

# Print the plot
print(pcoa_plot)

Functional metabolic pathways
# Make a new TSE for pathways
tse_pathways <- altExp(tse, "pathways")

# Perform multidimensional scaling (MDS) using Bray-Curtis dissimilarity on pathways relative abundance data
tse_pathways <- addMDS(
    tse_pathways, 
    FUN = getDissimilarity, 
    method = "bray", 
    assay.type = "cpm", 
    name = "MDS_bray"
)

# Extract coordinates
mds_coords <- reducedDims(tse_pathways)$MDS_bray

# Calculate explained variance
e <- attr(reducedDims(tse_pathways)$MDS_bray, "eig")
rel_eig <- e / sum(e[e > 0])
axis1_pct <- round(100 * rel_eig[[1]], 1)
axis2_pct <- round(100 * rel_eig[[2]], 1)
print("axis1_pct")
## [1] "axis1_pct"
print(axis1_pct)
## [1] 32.6
print("axis2_pct")
## [1] "axis2_pct"
print(axis2_pct)
## [1] 17.3
# Create data frame for plotting
pcoa_df <- data.frame(
  Axis1 = mds_coords[,1],
  Axis2 = mds_coords[,2],
  SampleName = rownames(mds_coords)
)

# Add category to the data frame for plotting
pcoa_df$Category <- colData(tse_pathways)$Category

# Plot PCoA with 95% CI ellipses
pcoa_plot_pathways <- ggplot(
  pcoa_df,
  aes(x = Axis1, y = Axis2, color = Category)
) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(fill = Category),
               type = "t",
               level = 0.95,
               geom = "polygon",
               alpha = 0.15,
               color = NA) +
  stat_ellipse(type = "t", level = 0.95, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal"
    ) +
  labs(
    x = "PCoA 1 (32.6%)",
    y = "PCoA 2 (17.3%)",
    color = "Schistosomiasis category",
    fill = "Schistosomiasis category",
    title = "Metabolic pathways"
  )

# Add boxplots to display differences between groups
pcoa_plot_pathways <- ggMarginal(pcoa_plot_pathways, type = "boxplot", groupFill = TRUE)

# Save the plot
ggsave("Figures/pcoa_plot_metabolic_pathways.png", pcoa_plot_pathways, width = 4.2, height = 3.5)

# Print the plot
print(pcoa_plot_pathways)

PERMANOVA

Genus-level composition

# Prep the data (genus level)
tse_genus <- altExp(tse, "genus")
tse_genus <- transformAssay(tse_genus, assay.type = "mpa", method = "relabundance")
colData(tse_genus)$Piped_water <- ifelse(colData(tse_genus)$drinking_water == "Piped", "Yes", "No")
colData(tse_genus)$age_group <- cut(
  colData(tse_genus)$Age,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 10, Inf),
  labels = c("6-10", "11-16")
)

# Set seed
set.seed(123)

# PERMANOVA
permanova_genus <- getPERMANOVA(
    tse_genus,
    assay.type = "relabundance",
    method = "bray",
    formula = x ~ Category + age_group + Sex + Giardia + abx_6mo + Piped_water,
    permutations = 9999
)
permanova_genus

# Import ARG assembly data
ARGs_assembly <- read.csv("Data/ARGs_assembly_summary.csv", check.names = FALSE)

# Apply transformations to all columns except 'Isolate' names so ARGs are present (1) or absent (0)
ARGs_assembly[, -1] <- lapply(ARGs_assembly[, -1], function(x) {
  ifelse(is.na(x) | x == "." | x == "", 0, 1)
})

# Capitalize first letter
colnames(ARGs_assembly) <- sapply(colnames(ARGs_assembly), function(x) {
  paste0(toupper(substring(x, 1, 1)), substring(x, 2))
})

# Mutate the data to have Sample and ARG columns
ARGs_assembly_long <- ARGs_assembly %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Sample,
    names_to = "ARG",
    values_to = "Presence"
  )

# Filter for only relevant rows (where presence is 1)
ARGs_assembly_long <- ARGs_assembly_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(Presence == 1) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Presence)

# Print all unique AMR determinants in data set
(colnames(ARGs_assembly)[-1])

# Define the AMR classes and their associated genes
aminoglycoside = "Aac|Ant|Aph|Rmt"
beta_lactam = "ACI|Cep|Cfx|OXA|TEM"
beta_lactam_carbapenem = "Cfi"
chloramphenicol = "Cat"
fosfomycin = "Fos"
glycopeptide = "Van"
macrolide = "Mef"
macrolide_streptogramin_B = "Msr"
MLSB = "Erm"
nitroimidazole = "Nim"
quinolone = "Qnr|Qep"
sulfonamide = "Sul"
tetracycline = "Tet"
trimethoprim = "Dfr"

# Calculate prevalence (% of samples) and assign ARG classes
ARG_prevalence_assembly <- ARGs_assembly_long %>%
  distinct(Sample, ARG) %>%                 # ensures each sample contributes once per ARG
  dplyr::count(ARG, name = "Count") %>%
  mutate(
    Percent = 100 * Count / 36,
    class = case_when(
      str_detect(ARG, aminoglycoside) ~ "Aminoglycoside",
      str_detect(ARG, beta_lactam) ~ "Beta-lactam",
      str_detect(ARG, beta_lactam_carbapenem) ~ "Beta-lactam (carbapenem)",
      str_detect(ARG, chloramphenicol) ~ "Chloramphenicol",
      str_detect(ARG, fosfomycin) ~ "Fosfomycin",
      str_detect(ARG, glycopeptide) ~ "Glycopeptide",
      str_detect(ARG, macrolide) ~ "Macrolide",
      str_detect(ARG, macrolide_streptogramin_B) ~ "Macrolide-streptogramin B",
      str_detect(ARG, MLSB) ~ "MLSB",
      str_detect(ARG, nitroimidazole) ~ "Nitroimidazole",
      str_detect(ARG, quinolone) ~ "Quinolone",
      str_detect(ARG, sulfonamide) ~ "Sulfonamide",
      str_detect(ARG, tetracycline) ~ "Tetracycline",
      str_detect(ARG, trimethoprim) ~ "Trimethoprim",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Reorder ARGs for plotting: first by class, then by count (highest to lowest)
ARG_prevalence_assembly <- ARG_prevalence_assembly %>%
  arrange(class, desc(Count)) %>%
  mutate(ARG = factor(ARG, levels = ARG))

# Reverse the order of classes and ARGs for top-to-bottom plotting
ARG_prevalence_assembly <- ARG_prevalence_assembly %>%
  mutate(class = factor(class, levels = sort(unique(class)))) %>%
  mutate(ARG = factor(ARG, levels = rev(ARG[order(ARG_prevalence_assembly$class, -ARG_prevalence_assembly$Count)])))

# Create the bar plot
AMR_assembly_plot <- ggplot(ARG_prevalence_assembly, aes(y = ARG, x = Percent, fill = class)) +
  geom_bar(color = "black", linewidth = 0.3, stat = "identity") +
  labs(y = "AMR determinant", x = "% of samples") +
  theme_minimal() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title = "Class")) +  
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA)
        ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#1b9e77", "#fdbf6f", "#7570b3", "#d95f02",
                   "#66a61e", "#e6ab02", "#a6761d", "#e7298a",
                   "#1f78b4", "#b2df8a", "#fb9a99", "#666666",
                   "#cab2d6", "#ffff99")) 

# Save the plot
ggsave("figures/AMR_assembly_plot.png", AMR_assembly_plot, height = 5, width = 10, dpi = 600)

Differential abundance analysis

Phylum

# Get data for various differential analyses
tse_da_phylum <- altExp(tse, "phylum")

# Transform relative abundance scale to range from 0-1
tse_da_phylum <- transformAssay(tse_da_phylum, assay.type = "mpa", method = "relabundance")

# Retain features exceeding 0.1% relative abundance in >25% of samples
relab <- assay(tse_da_phylum, "relabundance")
keep <- rowMeans(relab > 0.001, na.rm = TRUE) > 0.25
tse_da_phylum <- tse_da_phylum[keep, ]

# Convert to factor variables
colData(tse_da_phylum)$Category <- factor(colData(tse_da_phylum)$Category, levels = c("Control", "UGS", "ZIS"))
colData(tse_da_phylum)$MatchID <- factor(colData(tse_da_phylum)$MatchID)

# Run MaAsLin2
## Category as fixed effect
## MatchID included for random intercept (controls for matching of age, sex, giadiasis)
## Run in 'invisible' mode to prevent printing all output logs
invisible(
  capture.output(
    Maaslin2(
      input_data = assay(tse_da_phylum, "relabundance"),
      input_metadata = as.data.frame(colData(tse_da_phylum)),
      min_abundance = 0,       # Already filtered
      min_prevalence = 0,      # Already filtered
      fixed_effects = "Category",
      random_effects = "MatchID",
      reference = "Category,Control",
      normalization = "NONE",  # Already TSS normalised
      transform = "LOG",
      correction = "BH",       # Required, but replaced below
      plot_heatmap = FALSE,
      plot_scatter = FALSE,
      output = "maaslin2_phylum_output"
    ),
    file = NULL
  )
)
## boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular')
## boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular')
## boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular')
# Extract significant results with contrast-specific q-values
maaslin_phylum_res <- read.delim("maaslin2_phylum_output/all_results.tsv", header = TRUE, sep = "\t") |>
  filter(
    metadata == "Category",
    value %in% c("UGS", "ZIS")
  ) |>
  group_by(value) |>
  mutate(
    qval = p.adjust(pval, method = "BH"),
    reject = qval < 0.10
  ) |>
  ungroup()
sig_daa_phylum <- maaslin_phylum_res |>
  filter(reject)
if (nrow(sig_daa_phylum) == 0) {
  message("No significant results")
} else {
  print(sig_daa_phylum)
}
## No significant results

Secondary analysis with LinDA

# LinDA expects features in rows and samples in columns
linda_abund <- assay(tse_da_phylum, "relabundance")
linda_meta  <- as.data.frame(colData(tse_da_phylum))

# Ensure abundance columns and metadata rows are identically ordered
stopifnot(all(colnames(linda_abund) %in% rownames(linda_meta)))
linda_meta <- linda_meta[colnames(linda_abund), , drop = FALSE]

# Set reference levels
linda_meta$Category <- factor(
    linda_meta$Category,
    levels = c("Control", "UGS", "ZIS")
)
linda_meta$MatchID <- factor(linda_meta$MatchID)

# Fit LinDA mixed-effects models
linda_phylum <- linda(
    feature.dat = linda_abund,
    meta.dat = linda_meta,
    formula = "~ Category + (1 | MatchID)",
    feature.dat.type = "proportion",
    alpha = 0.10
)
## 0  features are filtered!
## The filtered data has  36  samples and  11  features will be tested!
## Fit linear mixed effects models ...
## Completed.
# Get significant results
linda_phylum_res <- bind_rows(
  linda_phylum$output$`CategoryZIS` |>
    filter(reject) |>
    rownames_to_column("feature") |>
    mutate(comparison = "ZIS vs Control"),

  linda_phylum$output$CategoryUGS |>
    filter(reject) |>
    rownames_to_column("feature") |>
    mutate(comparison = "UGS vs Control")
)
if (nrow(linda_phylum_res) == 0) {
  message("No significant results")
} else {
  print(linda_phylum_res)
}
## No significant results

    linda_meta$Category,

)

Features associated with ZIS - Brachyspira

# Prepare Brachyspira features for plotting
tse_species <- altExp(tse, "species")
tse_genus <- altExp(tse, "genus")

# Name features
genus_features <- "g__Brachyspira"
species_features <- c(
  "s__Brachyspira_aalborgi",
  "s__Brachyspira_pilosicoli")

# Combine selected genus- and species-level rows
brachyspira_features_tse <- rbind(
    tse_genus[genus_features, ],
    tse_species[species_features, ]
)

# Define feature order for plotting
feature_order <- c(
  "g__Brachyspira",
  "s__Brachyspira_aalborgi",
  "s__Brachyspira_pilosicoli"
)

# Feature labels: italicise taxon names
feature_labels <- as_labeller(
  c(
    "g__Brachyspira" = "italic('Brachyspira')",
    "s__Brachyspira_aalborgi" = "italic('B. aalborgi')",
    "s__Brachyspira_pilosicoli" = "italic('B. pilosicoli')"
  ),
  label_parsed
)

## ----------------
## Prepare infection-intensity data

# Retain only intestinal schistosomiasis cases
brachyspira_features_IS <- brachyspira_features_tse[
  ,
  brachyspira_features_tse$Category == "ZIS"
]

# Infection intensity (Schis gen Ct normalized using PhHV Ct internal amplification control)
colData(brachyspira_features_IS)$infection_intensity <-
  2^(-(colData(brachyspira_features_IS)$Faecal_schis_gen_Cq - colData(brachyspira_features_IS)$PhHV_Ct))

# Extract relative abundances in long format
abund_df <- assay(
  brachyspira_features_IS,
  "mpa"
)[feature_order, , drop = FALSE] %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("feature") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -feature,
    names_to = "sample_id",
    values_to = "relabundance"
  )

# Extract sample metadata
meta_df <- colData(brachyspira_features_IS) %>%
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("sample_id")

# Merge abundance and metadata
plot_df <- abund_df %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    meta_df,
    by = "sample_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    feature = factor(
      feature,
      levels = feature_order
    )
  )

# Add log2 transformation for IS infection intensity
plot_df <- abund_df |>
  dplyr::left_join(meta_df, by = "sample_id") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    log_intensity = log2(infection_intensity)
  )

# Spearman correlations
results <- lapply(
  feature_order,
  function(taxon) {

    df_tax <- plot_df %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        feature == taxon,
        !is.na(infection_intensity),
        !is.na(relabundance)
      )

    cor_test <- cor.test(
      df_tax$relabundance,
      df_tax$infection_intensity,
      method = "spearman",
      exact = FALSE
    )

    data.frame(
      feature = taxon,
      rho = unname(cor_test$estimate),
      p_value = cor_test$p.value,
      n = nrow(df_tax)
    )
  }
) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    feature = factor(
      feature,
      levels = feature_order
    ),
    label = paste0(
      "rho = ",
      sprintf("%.2f", rho),
      "\np = ",
      sprintf("%.3f", p_value)
    )
  )


## ----------------
## Plots

# Shared high-contrast age colour scale
age_colour_scale <- scale_colour_viridis_c(
  option = "plasma",
  direction = 1,
  limits = c(6, 15),
  breaks = c(6, 15),
  labels = c("6", "15"),
  name = "Age",
  oob = scales::squish,
  guide = guide_colourbar(
    title.position = "top",
    title.hjust = 0.5,
    barwidth = grid::unit(4, "cm"),
    barheight = grid::unit(0.35, "cm")
  )
)

# Shared shapes for sex scale
sex_shape_scale <- scale_shape_manual(
  name = "Sex",
  values = c(
    "Female" = 16,
    "Male" = 17
  ),
  guide = guide_legend(
    title.position = "top",
    title.hjust = 0.5,
    nrow = 1,
    byrow = TRUE
  )
)

# Relative abundance plot with prevalence bar per category
relabundance_plot_top <- plotBoxplot(
  brachyspira_features_tse,
  features = feature_order,
  assay.type = "mpa",
  x = "Category",
  color = "Age",
  shape = "Sex",
  facet.by = "rownames",
  add.proportion = TRUE,
  point.offset = "quasirandom",
  point.size = 2,
  point.alpha = 0.6,
  box.alpha = 0.15
) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~rownames,
    nrow = 1,
    labeller = feature_labels
  ) +
  age_colour_scale +
  sex_shape_scale +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-0.2, 1.51)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Relative abundance (%)"
  ) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 20,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      colour = "grey90",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(5.5, 5.5, 2, 5.5)
  )

# Relative abundance versus infection intensity plot
intensity_plot_bottom <- ggplot(
  plot_df,
  aes(
    x = log_intensity,
    y = relabundance,
    colour = Age,
    shape = Sex
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    alpha = 0.6,
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(
      x = log_intensity,
      y = relabundance,
      group = 1
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE,
    linewidth = 0.5,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = results,
    aes(
      x = -Inf,
      y = Inf,
      label = label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = -0.15,
    vjust = 1.25,
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~feature,
    nrow = 1,
    drop = FALSE,
    labeller = feature_labels
  ) +
  age_colour_scale +

# Import pairwise strain analysis data and add pair variable
strainphlan_pairwise_SGB_data <- read.csv("Data/Strainphlan_pairwise_SGB_data.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    Pair = paste(
      pmin(Sample1, Sample2), 
      "×", 
      pmax(Sample1, Sample2)
    )
  )

metadata <- as.data.frame(
  colData(tse)[, c("ID", "Category", "Age", "Sex", "drinking_water", "Giardia")]
) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Piped_water = drinking_water) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Piped_water = ifelse(Piped_water == "Piped", "Yes", "No")
  )

# Import list of SGBs where strain-sharing analysis was possible
strain_sharing_sgbs <- readLines("Data/strain_sharing_sgbs.txt")

# Import within-village transmission event data and add pair variable
strain_sharing_events <- read.csv("data/strain_sharing_events.csv") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("^E", Sample1)) %>% # Removes external training samples (Blantyre)
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("^E", Sample2)) %>% # Removes external training samples (Blantyre)
  mutate(
    Pair = paste(
      pmin(Sample1, Sample2), 
      "×", 
      pmax(Sample1, Sample2)
    )
  )

# Generate dataframe for pairwise participant information and strain-sharing
pairs <- strainphlan_pairwise_SGB_data %>%
  filter(SGB %in% strain_sharing_sgbs) %>%
  group_by(Pair) %>%
  summarise(
    shared_SGBs = n(),
    distance_m = dplyr::first(distance_m),
    same_household =dplyr::first(same_household),
    Sample1 = dplyr::first(Sample1),
    Sample2 = dplyr::first(Sample2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Identidy pairwise strains shared
strain_sharing_pairs <- strain_sharing_events %>%
  group_by(Pair) %>%
  summarise(
    strains_shared = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Add the number of strains shared to pairs dataframe
pairs <- pairs %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    strain_sharing_pairs %>% dplyr::select(Pair, strains_shared),
    by = "Pair"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    strains_shared = tidyr::replace_na(strains_shared, 0)
  )

# Add strain-sharing rates
pairs <- pairs %>%
  mutate(strain_sharing_rate = strains_shared / shared_SGBs)

# Exclude same household comparisons
pairs <- pairs %>%
  filter(same_household != "Yes")

# Stats on number of shared SGBs and strain-sharing rate (ensure all are minimum 10 for robust strain-sharing inference)
print("No. shared SGBs")

print("strain-level microbiome similarity")
## [1] "strain-level microbiome similarity"
summary(pairs$strain_sharing_rate)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.

print("total no. strain-sharing events")

nrow(strain_sharing_events)

# Define function to add metadata combinations to pair data
add_pairwise_contrasts <- function(pairs, metadata) {
  
  metadata <- metadata %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Schisto = ifelse(Category == "Control", "No", "Yes")
    )
  
  pairs %>%
    dplyr::left_join(metadata, by = c("Sample1" = "ID")) %>%
    dplyr::rename_with(
      ~ paste0(.x, "1"),
      c(Category, Age, Sex, Piped_water, Giardia, Schisto)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(metadata, by = c("Sample2" = "ID")) %>%
    dplyr::rename_with(
      ~ paste0(.x, "2"),
      c(Category, Age, Sex, Piped_water, Giardia, Schisto)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      age_diff = abs(Age1 - Age2),
      
      schisto_contrast = dplyr::case_when(
        Schisto1 == "Yes" & Schisto2 == "Yes" ~ "Both infected",
        Schisto1 == "No"  & Schisto2 == "No"  ~ "Neither infected",
        TRUE ~ "Discordant"
      ),
      
      category_key = paste(
        pmin(Category1, Category2),
        pmax(Category1, Category2),
        sep = " × "
      ),
      
      category_contrast = dplyr::recode(
        category_key,
        "Control × Control" = "Control",
        "Control × UGS" = "C × U",
        "Control × ZIS" = "C × Z",
        "UGS × UGS" = "UGS",
        "UGS × ZIS" = "U × Z",
        "ZIS × ZIS" = "ZIS",
        .default = NA_character_
      ),
      
      sex_contrast = dplyr::case_when(
        Sex1 == "Female" & Sex2 == "Female" ~ "Both female",
        Sex1 == "Male"   & Sex2 == "Male"   ~ "Both male",
        TRUE ~ "Discordant"
      ),
      
      piped_water_contrast = dplyr::case_when(
        Piped_water1 == "Yes" & Piped_water2 == "Yes" ~ "Both piped",
        Piped_water1 == "No"  & Piped_water2 == "No"  ~ "Neither piped",
        TRUE ~ "Discordant"
      ),
      
      giardia_contrast = dplyr::case_when(
        Giardia1 == "Yes" & Giardia2 == "Yes" ~ "Both infected",
        Giardia1 == "No"  & Giardia2 == "No"  ~ "Neither infected",
        TRUE ~ "Discordant"
      ),
      
      schisto_contrast = factor(
        schisto_contrast,
        levels = c("Neither infected", "Discordant", "Both infected")
      ),
      
      category_contrast = factor(
        category_contrast,
        levels = c("Control", "C × U", "C × Z", "UGS", "U × Z", "ZIS")
      ),
      
      sex_contrast = factor(
        sex_contrast,
        levels = c("Both female", "Discordant", "Both male")
      ),
      
      piped_water_contrast = factor(
        piped_water_contrast,
        levels = c("Neither piped", "Discordant", "Both piped")
      ),
      
      giardia_contrast = factor(
        giardia_contrast,
        levels = c("Neither infected", "Discordant", "Both infected")
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-category_key)
}

# Generate pairwise comparison dataframe
pairs <- add_pairwise_contrasts(
  pairs = pairs,
  metadata = metadata
)

# Convert distance between households from metres to 100m
## (based on previous trends of E. coli strain sharing in the same village)
pairs <- pairs %>%
  mutate(distance_100m = (distance_m/100))

# Convert age difference to categories
pairs <- pairs %>%
  mutate(age_diff = case_when(
    age_diff < 2 ~ "<2",
    age_diff >= 2 & age_diff <= 3 ~ "2-3",
    age_diff >= 4 & age_diff <= 5 ~ "4-5",
    age_diff >= 6 & age_diff <= 7 ~ "6-7",
    age_diff > 7 ~ "8-9"
  ))
pairs <- pairs %>%
  mutate(age_diff = factor(age_diff, levels = c("<2", "2-3", "4-5", "6-7", "8-9")))
# Define colour palette for plots
pair_type_cols <- setNames(
  viridis::viridis(3),
  c("Neither infected", "Discordant", "Both infected")
)

Schistosomiasis

# KW test for differing strain-sharing rates within and between disease/healthy groups
kruskal.test(strain_sharing_rate ~ schisto_contrast, data = pairs)
## 
##  Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data:  strain_sharing_rate by schisto_contrast
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 13.42, df = 2, p-value = 0.001218
# Post hoc Dunn test
dunnTest(strain_sharing_rate ~ schisto_contrast, data = pairs, method = "bh")
##   Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test
## 
## data: x and g
## Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 13.4203, df = 2, p-value = 0
## 
## 
##                      Dunn's Pairwise Comparison of x by g                     
##                              (Benjamini-Hochberg)                             
## Col Mean-│
## Row Mean │   Both inf   Discorda
## ─────────┼──────────────────────
## Discorda │   3.009265
##          │     0.0079*
##          │
## Neither  │   2.928693   1.078528
##          │     0.0051*    0.2808 
## 
## FDR = 0.05
## Reject Ho if p ≤ FDR with stopping rule, where p = Pr(|Z| ≥ |z|)
## Dunn (1964) Kruskal-Wallis multiple comparison
## 
##   p-values adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg method.
##                         Comparison        Z     P.unadj       P.adj
## 1       Both infected - Discordant 3.009265 0.002618805 0.007856416
## 2 Both infected - Neither infected 2.928694 0.003403898 0.005105847
## 3    Discordant - Neither infected 1.078528 0.280798190 0.280798190
# Significance labels for plot
sig_df <- tribble(
  ~group1,             ~group2,          ~label,  ~y.position,
  "Neither infected",  "Both infected",  "**",    40,
  "Discordant",       "Both infected",  "**",    38,
)

# Get medians for each group
median_df <- pairs %>%
  dplyr::group_by(schisto_contrast) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = median(100 * strain_sharing_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    label = sprintf("%.1f%%", med)
  )

# Plot strain-sharing rates within groups
strain_sharing_schisto_contrast <- ggplot(pairs,
                                          aes(x = schisto_contrast,
                                              y = 100 * strain_sharing_rate,
                                              colour = schisto_contrast)
                                          ) +
  geom_quasirandom(width = 0.3, alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 43)) +
  geom_text(
    data = median_df,
    aes(x = schisto_contrast, y = 42.5, label = label),
    colour = "black",
    size = 3,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
  stat_pvalue_manual(
    sig_df,
    label = "label",
    xmin = "group1",
    xmax = "group2",
    y.position = "y.position",
    tip.length = 0.01,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_colour_manual(name = "Pair schistosomiasis status", values = pair_type_cols, drop = FALSE) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Schistosomiasis",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Strain-level microbiome similarity (%)"
  )

# Save the plot
ggsave("Figures/strain_sharing_schisto_contrast.png", strain_sharing_schisto_contrast,
       width = 3.5, height = 4, dpi = 600)

# Print the plot
strain_sharing_schisto_contrast

# Participant level summary statistics

# Make data symmetric (long format)
pairs_long <- bind_rows(
  pairs %>%
    transmute(
      sample = Sample1,
      other  = Sample2,
      group  = Schisto1,
      other_group = Schisto2,
      strain_sharing_rate
    ),
  pairs %>%
    transmute(
      sample = Sample2,
      other  = Sample1,
      group  = Schisto2,
      other_group = Schisto1,
      strain_sharing_rate
    )
)

# Define within vs between group compairson
pairs_long <- pairs_long %>%
  mutate(
    comparison = ifelse(group == other_group, "within", "between")
  )

# Summarise strain_sharing
summary_df <- pairs_long %>%
  group_by(sample, comparison) %>%
  summarise(
    median_sharing = median(strain_sharing_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_pairs = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Generate mmedian strain-sharing statistics within and between groups per sample
wide_df <- summary_df %>%
  dplyr::select(sample, comparison, median_sharing) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = comparison,
    values_from = median_sharing
  ) %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(grepl("^C", sample), "Control", "Schisto")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diff = within - between)

# Effect size
wide_df %>%
group_by(group) %>%
summarise(
    median = median(diff),
    IQR = IQR(diff)
)
# Wilcoxon rank sum test
wilcox.test(diff ~ group, data = wide_df)
## 
##  Wilcoxon rank sum exact test
## 
## data:  diff by group
## W = 57, p-value = 0.002742
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

## Both mal │  -2.959157
##          │     0.0093*
##          │
## Discorda │  -1.606759   1.934020
##          │     0.1081     0.0797 
## 
## FDR = 0.05
## Reject Ho if p ≤ FDR with stopping rule, where p = Pr(|Z| ≥ |z|)
## Dunn (1964) Kruskal-Wallis multiple comparison
## 
##   p-values adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg method.
##                 Comparison         Z     P.unadj       P.adj
## 1  Both female - Both male -2.959158 0.003084812 0.009254436
## 2 Both female - Discordant -1.606760 0.108107102 0.108107102
## 3   Both male - Discordant  1.934020 0.053110667 0.079666001

# Participant level summary statistics

# Make data symmetric (long format)
pairs_long <- bind_rows(
  pairs %>%
    transmute(
      sample = Sample1,
      other  = Sample2,
      group  = Piped_water1,
      other_group = Piped_water2,
      strain_sharing_rate
    ),
  pairs %>%
    transmute(
      sample = Sample2,
      other  = Sample1,
      group  = Piped_water2,
      other_group = Piped_water1,
      strain_sharing_rate
    )
)

# Define within vs between group compairson
pairs_long <- pairs_long %>%
  mutate(
    comparison = ifelse(group == other_group, "within", "between")
  )

# Summarise strain_sharing
summary_df <- pairs_long %>%
  group_by(sample, comparison) %>%
  summarise(
    median_sharing = median(strain_sharing_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_pairs = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Generate median strain-sharing statistics within and between groups per sample
wide_df <- summary_df %>%
  dplyr::select(sample, comparison, median_sharing) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = comparison,
    values_from = median_sharing
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    metadata %>%
      dplyr::select(ID, Sex),
    by = c("sample" = "ID")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(group = Sex) %>%
  mutate(diff = within - between)

# Effect size
wide_df %>%
group_by(group) %>%
summarise(
    median = median(diff),
    IQR = IQR(diff)
)
# Wilcoxon rank sum test
wilcox.test(diff ~ group, data = wide_df)
## 
##  Wilcoxon rank sum exact test
## 
## data:  diff by group
## W = 185, p-value = 0.391
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

# Add references

# Add labels

  mutate(
    label = case_when(
      term == "category_contrastC × C" ~ "Control × Control",
      term == "category_contrastC × U" ~ "Control × UGS",
      term == "category_contrastC × Z" ~ "Control × ZIS",
      term == "category_contrastUGS" ~ "UGS × UGS",

    variable = case_when(

      grepl("^sex", term) ~ "Sex",
      grepl("^piped", term) ~ "Water",
      grepl("^distance", term) ~ "Distance"
    ),

    reference = is.na(conf.low)

# Add alphabetical factor levels for variable

Permutations

# Set seed
set.seed(123)

# Number of permutations to perform for each covariate
n_perm <- 1000

# Original model
model_nb <- glm.nb(
  strains_shared ~
    category_contrast +
    age_diff +
    sex_contrast +
    piped_water_contrast +
    distance_100m +
    offset(log(shared_SGBs)),
  data = pairs
)

# Original log-likelihood
ll_orig <- as.numeric(logLik(model_nb))

# Storage
ll_perms <- data.frame(matrix(nrow = n_perm, ncol = 5))

colnames(ll_perms) <- c(
  "category_contrast",
  "age_diff",
  "sex_contrast",
  "piped_water_contrast",
  "distance_100m"
)

# Category Contrast
for (i in 1:n_perm) {
  dat_permuted <- pairs
  dat_permuted$category_contrast <- sample(dat_permuted$category_contrast)

  model_perm <- glm.nb(
    strains_shared ~ category_contrast + age_diff + sex_contrast +
      piped_water_contrast + distance_100m + offset(log(shared_SGBs)),
    data = dat_permuted
  )

  ll_perms$category_contrast[i] <- as.numeric(logLik(model_perm))
}

# Age difference
for (i in 1:n_perm) {
  dat_permuted <- pairs
  dat_permuted$age_diff <- sample(dat_permuted$age_diff)

  model_perm <- glm.nb(
    strains_shared ~ category_contrast + age_diff + sex_contrast +
      piped_water_contrast + distance_100m + offset(log(shared_SGBs)),
    data = dat_permuted
  )

  ll_perms$age_diff[i] <- as.numeric(logLik(model_perm))
}

# Sex contrast
for (i in 1:n_perm) {
  dat_permuted <- pairs
  dat_permuted$sex_contrast <- sample(dat_permuted$sex_contrast)

  model_perm <- glm.nb(
    strains_shared ~ category_contrast + age_diff + sex_contrast +
      piped_water_contrast + distance_100m + offset(log(shared_SGBs)),
    data = dat_permuted
  )

  ll_perms$sex_contrast[i] <- as.numeric(logLik(model_perm))
}

# Piped water contrast
for (i in 1:n_perm) {
  dat_permuted <- pairs
  dat_permuted$piped_water_contrast <- sample(dat_permuted$piped_water_contrast)

  model_perm <- glm.nb(
    strains_shared ~ category_contrast + age_diff + sex_contrast +
      piped_water_contrast + distance_100m + offset(log(shared_SGBs)),
    data = dat_permuted
  )

  ll_perms$piped_water_contrast[i] <- as.numeric(logLik(model_perm))
}

# Distance between households (per 100 m)
for (i in 1:n_perm) {
  dat_permuted <- pairs
  dat_permuted$distance_100m <- sample(dat_permuted$distance_100m)

  model_perm <- glm.nb(
    strains_shared ~ category_contrast + age_diff + sex_contrast +
      piped_water_contrast + distance_100m + offset(log(shared_SGBs)),
    data = dat_permuted
  )

  ll_perms$distance_100m[i] <- as.numeric(logLik(model_perm))
}

# Convert to importance: loss in log-likelihood
ll_importance <- ll_orig - ll_perms

# Rename for plotting
colnames(ll_importance) <- c(
  "Schistosomiasis\ncategory",
  "Age\ndifference",
  "Sex",
  "Piped drinking\nwater",
  "Household\ndistance"
)

# Longer data longer
ll_importance <- ll_importance %>%
  pivot_longer(everything())

# Plot feature importance
feature_importance_plot <- ggplot(ll_importance, aes(
    x = reorder(name, value, median),
    y = value,
    colour = name
  )) +
  ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(size = 0.2,alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(logLik[orig] - logLik[perm])
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

TRACS SNP analysis

# Import data for pairs sharing strains with <100 SNPs per 5 Mb (<0.002%)
tracs_similar_pairs <- read.csv("Data/TRACS_similar_pairs.csv")

# Create an order-independent participant pair ID
tracs_similar_pairs <- tracs_similar_pairs %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pair = ifelse(
      sampleA < sampleB,
      paste(sampleA, sampleB, sep = "_"),
      paste(sampleB, sampleA, sep = "_")
    )
  )

# Remove duplicate comparisons for the same participant pair and species
# Where duplicates occur, retain the comparison with the lowest SNP divergence
tracs_similar_pairs <- tracs_similar_pairs %>%
  dplyr::arrange(percentage) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(pair, genus, species, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Generate mutually exclusive categories for SNP divergence
tracs_similar_pairs <- tracs_similar_pairs %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    SNP_perc_cat = dplyr::case_when(
      percentage < 0.0002 ~ "<0.0002%",
      percentage < 0.0005 ~ "<0.0005%",
      percentage < 0.002  ~ "<0.002%"
    ),
    SNP_perc_cat = factor(
      SNP_perc_cat,
      levels = c(
        "<0.0002%",
        "<0.0005%",
        "<0.002%"
      )
    )
  )

# Summarise participant pair-species comparisons by genus and species
tracs_species_summary <- tracs_similar_pairs %>%
  dplyr::count(genus, species, SNP_perc_cat, name = "n") %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    tidyr::nesting(genus, species),
    SNP_perc_cat,
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = SNP_perc_cat,
    values_from = n
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Total = rowSums(
      dplyr::across(c("<0.0002%", "<0.0005%", "<0.002%"))
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(genus, species)

tracs_species_summary

# Import data
esbl_sac <- read.csv("Data/SAC_schisto_ESBL_Ec.csv", na.strings = c("", "NA"))
esbl_sac$Sex <- as.factor(esbl_sac$Sex)
esbl_sac$Schistosomiasis <- as.factor(esbl_sac$Schistosomiasis)
esbl_sac$piped_water <- as.factor(esbl_sac$piped_water)
esbl_sac$abx_6mo <- as.factor(esbl_sac$abx_6mo)
esbl_sac$freshwater_contact <- as.factor(esbl_sac$freshwater_contact)
esbl_sac$stagnant_water_contact <- as.factor(esbl_sac$stagnant_water_contact)

# Re-level water contact variables
esbl_sac$freshwater_contact <- dplyr::case_when(
  esbl_sac$freshwater_contact %in% c("Monthly", "Never", "Yearly") ~ "Less than weekly",
  esbl_sac$freshwater_contact %in% c("Weekly", "Three times a week") ~ "Weekly but not daily",
  esbl_sac$freshwater_contact %in% c("More than once daily", "Once daily") ~ "At least daily",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)
esbl_sac$freshwater_contact <- factor(
  esbl_sac$freshwater_contact,
  levels = c(
    "Less than weekly",
    "Weekly but not daily",
    "At least daily"
  )
)
esbl_sac$stagnant_water_contact <- dplyr::case_when(
  esbl_sac$stagnant_water_contact %in% c("Every other month", "Monthly", "Never", "Yearly") ~ "Less than weekly",
  esbl_sac$stagnant_water_contact %in% c("Weekly", "Three times a week") ~ "Weekly but not daily",
  esbl_sac$stagnant_water_contact %in% c("More than once daily", "Once daily") ~ "At least daily",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)
esbl_sac$stagnant_water_contact <- factor(
  esbl_sac$stagnant_water_contact,
  levels = c(
    "Less than weekly",
    "Weekly but not daily",
    "At least daily"
  )
)

# Prevalence of ESBL-Ec colonisation in this SAC group
overall_events <- sum(esbl_sac$ESBL_Ec == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
overall_n <- sum(!is.na(esbl_sac$ESBL_Ec))
overall_prevalence <- overall_events / overall_n
scales::percent(overall_prevalence, accuracy = 0.01)
## [1] "48.18%"
# Function returning a 95% CI for one proportion
get_prop_ci <- function(x, n, conf.level = 0.95) {
  prop.test(
    x = x,
    n = n,
    conf.level = conf.level,
    correct = FALSE
  )$conf.int
}

# Prepare data to plot ESBL-Ec colonisation rates vs schisto/WASH variables
plot_dat <- esbl_sac %>%
  dplyr::select(
    ESBL_Ec,
    Schistosomiasis,
    piped_water,
    freshwater_contact,
    stagnant_water_contact
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -ESBL_Ec,
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Category"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Category), !is.na(ESBL_Ec)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Variable, Category) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    events = sum(ESBL_Ec == 1),
    n = dplyr::n(),
    Colonisation_rate = events / n,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rowwise() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    CI_lower = get_prop_ci(events, n)[1],
    CI_upper = get_prop_ci(events, n)[2]
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Variable = dplyr::recode(
      Variable,
      "freshwater_contact" =
        "c) Freshwater contact (river, stream, lake)",
      "piped_water" =
        "b) Primary drinking water source: piped water",
      "stagnant_water_contact" =
        "d) Stagnant water contact (pond, swamp, rice paddy)",
      "Schistosomiasis" =
        "a) Schistosomiasis"
    )
  )

# Generate plot of colonisation rates
ESBL_Ec_rate_plot <- ggplot(
  plot_dat,
  aes(x = Category, y = Colonisation_rate)
) +
  geom_col(
    fill = "steelblue",
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = CI_lower,
      ymax = CI_upper
    ),
    width = 0.15,
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      y = CI_upper,
      label = paste0(
        events, "/", n,
        "\n(",
        percent(Colonisation_rate, accuracy = 0.01),
        ")"
      )
    ),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~Variable,
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, 1),
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(
      "ESBL-producing " *
        italic("E. coli") *
        " gut colonisation rate"
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 20,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(5.5, 12, 5.5, 5.5)
  )

# Save the plot
ggsave("Figures/ESBL_Ec_rate_plot.png", ESBL_Ec_rate_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 600)

# Print the plot
print(ESBL_Ec_rate_plot)

# Schistosomiasis
tab <- table(esbl_sac$Schistosomiasis, esbl_sac$ESBL_Ec)
print("schistosomiasis")
## [1] "schistosomiasis"
chisq.test(tab)
## 
##  Pearson's Chi-squared test with Yates' continuity correction
## 
## data:  tab
## X-squared = 0.36722, df = 1, p-value = 0.5445
# Piped water
tab <- table(esbl_sac$piped_water, esbl_sac$ESBL_Ec)
print("piped drinking water")

chisq.test(tab)

## data:  tab

tab <- table(esbl_sac$freshwater_contact, esbl_sac$ESBL_Ec)
